text: In this month our record converges on one bill. On 2017-10-03, seventy-one of us said "child protection act" and seventy said "unborn child protection act." Sixty of us said "pain-capable unborn child"; fifty-nine said "pain-capable unborn child protection act" and "the pain-capable unborn"; fifty-eight said "the pain-capable unborn child"; fifty-seven said "the pain-capable unborn child protection act." The phrasing tightens as the count narrows, the same words layered across dozens of us on a single day. Later, on 2017-10-26, forty-nine of us said "public health emergency." That is the shape of the record from this era: one measure named in near-identical language by most of us at once, then a second, smaller alignment weeks on. We report it as it stands.

top_phrases.phrase: the pain-capable unborn child protection act
